items.title: The Spice Isle Advantages
items.text: Grenada offers a stable, English-speaking workforce with a law system based on English Common Law, making contracts familiar to US/UK firms.

items.title: Vacation Escalation
items.text: Note that statutory vacation increases from 2 weeks to 3 weeks after just one year of service.

items.title: Remote Work Sentiment
items.text: Grenada is increasingly popular for remote tech roles due to its Digital Nomad Visa (NDV) and reliable subsea fiber connectivity in major hubs.

faqs.question: Can I hire contractors through an EOR?
faqs.answer: EORs primarily focus on full-time employment. For contractors, a 'Contractor Management' service is typically used to handle compliance and payments.

faqs.question: What is the standard probation period?
faqs.answer: Probation is typically 3 to 6 months, during which notice periods are significantly shorter (often zero in the first few months).

faqs.question: Is insurance mandatory?
faqs.answer: NIS is mandatory. Private health insurance is common for executive roles as a top-up benefit.

faqs.question: Are 13th-month salaries required?
faqs.answer: No, a 13th-month bonus is not a statutory requirement in Grenada, though performance-based bonuses are common.

faqs.question: How is termination handled?
faqs.answer: Termination must follow the Employment Act, requiring notice and potentially severance pay for workers with over one year of service.

faqs.question: Can expatriates be hired through EOR?
faqs.answer: Yes, but they will require a valid work permit, which the EOR partner typically facilitates with the Ministry of Labour.

items.title: Maximum Insurable Earnings
items.text: NIS contributions are capped at XCD 5,200 per month. Income above this threshold does not incur further NIS charges.

items.title: Payment Frequency
items.text: Monthly pay cycles are standard for professional roles, while weekly or bi-weekly cycles are common for hospitality and agriculture.

items.title: Digital Payslips

items.title: Tax Compliance Certificates

faqs.question: What is the NIS contribution rate?
faqs.answer: For 2026, the employer pays 7.25% and the employee pays 6.25% of gross salary.

faqs.question: When is the payroll tax deadline?
faqs.answer: PAYE must be remitted to the Inland Revenue Department by the 15th of the following month.

faqs.question: Can payroll be processed in USD?
faqs.answer: While the salary may be denominated in USD, the actual payment and statutory reporting must be in XCD.

faqs.question: How are sick days paid?
faqs.answer: Employers typically pay for the first few days, after which the employee claims sickness benefit from the NIS.

faqs.question: Are there payroll software requirements?
faqs.answer: Systems should be able to generate the magnetic media files accepted by the IRD and NIS for monthly uploads.

faqs.question: What is the TD4 form?
faqs.answer: The TD4 is the annual certificate provided to employees showing total earnings and taxes withheld for the year.

faqs.question: Does this calculator include performance bonuses?
faqs.answer: Default calculations are based on base salary. You can add bonuses as a lump sum and they are taxed at marginal rates.

faqs.question: How often is this updated?
faqs.answer: We update NIS and PAYE rates annually, typically within Q1 following the Budget announcement.

faqs.question: Can I export the calculations?

faqs.question: What is the XCD personal allowance?
faqs.answer: The current annual personal allowance is XCD 36,000, which is deducted before PAYE calculation.

faqs.question: Does it calculate self-employment tax?
faqs.answer: This version is optimized for employer-employee relationships. Self-employed individuals have different NIS contribution requirements (usually 11%).

faqs.question: Is the 2026 NIS rate increase included?
faqs.answer: Yes, our calculator defaults to the combined 13.5% NIS rate (7.25% employer / 6.25% employee) for the 2026 fiscal year.
